test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper kept the marked price of an item at Rs. 500. He sold it at a scheme discount of 10% and 20% and got a profit of 25%. What was the cost price of the item?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net Discount % = 10 + 20 − (10 × 20 / 100) = 28%

Selling Price (SP) = 72% of 500 = 0.72 × 500 = Rs. 360

Ratio of CP : SP at 25% profit = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5

5 units = Rs. 360 ⇒ 1 unit = 72 ⇒ 4 units = 4 × 72 = Rs. 288

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 288.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price** (MP) = Rs. 500

Successive **Discounts** = 10% and 20%

**Profit percentage** = 25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd3d2b4092e63eaca1c81792c8757a23d43df1fb14a12e13970fa2f7ce661cfc.png] 

Calculation of **Selling Price** (SP) after successive discounts:

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 10)/100 × (100 − 20)/100

⇒ SP = 500 × 90/100 × 80/100

⇒ SP = 500 × 0.9 × 0.8

⇒ SP = 450 × 0.8 = Rs. 360

Calculation of **Cost Price** (CP) using Profit Percentage:

⇒ CP = (SP × 100) / (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP = (360 × 100) / (100 + 25)

⇒ CP = (360 × 100) / 125

⇒ CP = 360 / 1.25 = Rs. 288

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 288.**

**__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relation Formula

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Profit and Loss Base

Profit or loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price** (CP), while discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price** (MP).</p
